intro.title: Full VS Code inside Orkestr
intro.body: Orkestr can run VSCodium — the open-source build of VS Code — on your project folder. Extensions come from the Open VSX registry, so most popular extensions (languages, linters, themes, debuggers) work.

consent.title: Install VS Code (VSCodium)?
consent.subtitle: Downloaded on demand from the official VSCodium releases
consent.checksum: The SHA-256 checksum published with the release is verified before anything is unpacked.
consent.risk: VS Code extensions are third-party code. They run with the permissions of your OS user: they can read and change any of your files, start programs and use the network. Orkestr's permission rules and approvals do not apply to them. Install only extensions you trust.
consent.server: The VS Code server listens only on 127.0.0.1 and requires a secret token. By default it stops when no VS Code view has been open for a while.
consent.accept: I understand that extensions run as my user
consent.loadError: Could not get the release information: {{error}}

run.restarting: The VS Code server crashed and is restarting…
run.windowOpen: VS Code is open in its own window.
run.windowClosed: The VS Code window is closed. The server keeps running until it is stopped or idle.
run.why: VS Code opens in its own window so that its keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+P, Ctrl+Shift+P…) and its secure sign-in work reliably.
run.extensionsHint: Install extensions from the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X); they come from Open VSX. You can also drag a .vsix file into that view.
run.syncHint: VS Code edits the same folder: saved files show up in Orkestr's Code, Files and Git panels.

settings.title: VS Code
settings.dataDirHint: Server package, VS Code settings and extensions live here.
settings.autoStopDesc: Extensions run only while VS Code is used: the server stops when no VS Code panel or window has been open for the chosen time.
settings.autoRestartDesc: Restarts the server automatically (with increasing delays, at most 5 times in 10 minutes).
settings.uninstallBody: The server package is deleted and the server is stopped. Project files are not touched.
settings.purge: Also delete VS Code settings and installed extensions
settings.securityBody: VS Code extensions are third-party code running with your user's permissions, outside Orkestr's permission rules and approvals. The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 with a random token, stops with “Stop All AI” and when Orkestr exits.
settings.legal: Orkestr uses VSCodium (MIT license) and the Open VSX registry. The Microsoft Visual Studio Marketplace is not used.
